evidence.summary: login checks email and password via db.check and returns a JWT carrying sub (user id) and role, signed with a literal key in the code (value not copied; scan finding).
Header comment (a claim): JWT bearer tokens; posts publish immediately; anonymous posting allowed.
create_post refuses bodies over 10000 characters (ValueError), takes the author from the token if one is given, otherwise None, and inserts the post with no status field.
get_post reads a post by integer id with no authentication; comment gives the response as {id int, body str, author_id int or None}.
users model (SQL given as a comment): id integer primary key, email text, name text, role user|admin.
posts model (SQL given as a comment): id integer primary key, author_id integer null (null = anonymous), body text max 10000, created_at timestamp; no status column.
MIT licence: use without restriction, keep the notice.
No endpoint lists posts, so what the /posts screen shows is inferred only.
Token verification calls jwt.decode with a literal key and no algorithms argument.

architecture.frontend: client routes listed in a Python constant (frontend framework not shown)
architecture.backend: Python functions mapped to HTTP routes in a ROUTES dict; web framework and db layer not in the folder

workflows.name: Post straight to the forum (with or without an account)
edge_cases: no token: the post is anonymous

features.name: Sign in with a bearer token (JWT)
features.description: A user exchanges email and password for a signed JWT used as a bearer token.
features.observed_behaviour: POST /api/token returns {token} with sub and role claims.
features.business_logic: Signing key is a literal in the code; no expiry claim; decode passes no algorithms list.

features.name: Write a post (up to 10000 characters)
features.description: Create a post of at most 10000 characters.
features.observed_behaviour: POST /api/posts inserts the post; bodies over 10000 characters raise ValueError.

features.name: Instant publishing
features.description: Posts are visible as soon as they are created; there is no review step.
features.observed_behaviour: create_post inserts with no status and get_post returns any post, so a new post is readable at once.

features.name: Anonymous posting
features.description: Anyone can post without an account; the post has no author.
features.observed_behaviour: With no token, author_id is None and the post is still inserted.

features.name: Read a post (public)
features.description: Anyone can open a post by id without signing in.
features.observed_behaviour: GET /api/posts/<int:post_id> has no auth and returns id, body, author_id.

features.name: Post list screen
features.observed_behaviour: The client route exists; no list endpoint, so its content is not established.

entities.name: User
entities.description: A person who signs in to the forum (user or admin).

entities.name: Post
entities.description: A forum post, published as soon as it is written, optionally anonymous.

fields.name: author_id
fields.description: the user who wrote it; null means anonymous

auth.model: role claim in token (no permission checks in the code shown)

configuration.purpose: signs and verifies tokens; hard-coded literal in api.py, not configurable (value never copied)

error_handling.behaviour: ValueError('too long'); the HTTP status it becomes is not shown
jwt.decode raises; how that reaches the client is not shown

unknowns: Password storage and db.check: the db layer is not in the folder. Settled by its code.
Web framework, and how ROUTES and exceptions map to HTTP responses: not in the folder.

PyJWT version: no manifest. With PyJWT 2.x, jwt.decode without an algorithms argument raises, which would break signed-in posting; with 1.x it accepts any algorithm the token names. Which applies cannot be determined without a manifest (inferred from library knowledge, not observed).
What the admin role can do: ROLES lists it but no code checks any role.
Token expiry: none is set in the code shown; whether something else enforces one is unknown.
No list endpoint exists, so what the /posts screen shows is unknown.
The users and posts models are SQL given as comments; the real schema (constraints, uniqueness of email) is not shown.
